label: Screening candidate — found by data, not field-checked
about: Discover Jordan: Jordan covered with 10 km boxes, each measured like a hand-picked site. Climate: the NASA POWER cells that hold the box centre (the rule of the POWER point API used for the sites). Terrain: 441 Copernicus DEM samples per box, with the same statistics as data/terrain.json. Geology: the main rock from the IGME5000 map (1:5 million) at 25 points per box. The app scores every box against each Moon and Mars target with the same formula as the sites; boxes have no resources data, so that pillar is left out, and a box % can only be compared with a site % that also leaves resources out. Every box is a screening candidate: found by data, not field-checked, and not checked for access, protection or safety. Built by scripts/build_screening.py from data/raw/screening/stages/; the raw files are in data/raw/screening/ (see README.txt there).

grid.dlonFormula: dlat / cos(radians(31.28)): 10 km of longitude at 31.28 N
grid.idPattern: jo-rRRcCC (RR = row, CC = col, two digits each)
grid.bounds: s = south + row * dlat, n = south + (row + 1) * dlat, w = west + col * dlon, e = west + (col + 1) * dlon (degrees, not rounded)
grid.centre: lat = south + (row + 0.5) * dlat, lon = west + (col + 0.5) * dlon, rounded to 6 decimals
grid.inclusion: a box is kept when its centre (6 decimals) is inside the Natural Earth 10m v5.1.1 Jordan polygon (even-odd ray casting in longitude/latitude)
grid.inJordan: share of the box inside the polygon, 0 to 1, 4 decimals: exact clipping of the polygon by the box in longitude/latitude; 1 only when the boundary does not touch the box (a touching box shows at most 0.9999)
grid.borderKm: distance from the box centre to the nearest point of the polygon boundary, km, 2 decimals (local equirectangular projection, R = 6,371,008.8 m)
grid.pointToBox: row = floor((lat - south) / dlat), col = floor((lon - west) / dlon)
grid.coverage: 20519 of 21047 lattice points inside Jordan are in a box; the other 528 are within 14.2 km of the border (0.02 deg lattice)

boundary.source: Natural Earth 1:10m Cultural Vectors, Admin 0 - Countries
boundary.note: Natural Earth's de facto, generalised boundary of Jordan. It is indicative only and does not include the West Bank.

climate.periodLabel: The requested parameters are retrieved from a pre-computed climatological period (January 2001 - December 2025)
climate.periodValidated: values equal the project's 2001–2020 point files, 1092/1092, 2026-10-10
climate.rule: Each box takes the POWER cells that hold its centre, which is the rule of the POWER point API used for the hand-picked sites. MERRA-2 (T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, T2M_RANGE, RH2M, PRECTOTCORR, WS2M, PS, TS, TS_MAX, TS_MIN; 0.5 x 0.625 deg): lat_c = round(lat / 0.5) * 0.5, lon_c = -180 + round((lon + 180) / 0.625) * 0.625. CERES SYN1deg (ALLSKY_SRF_ALB, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, ALLSKY_SFC_UV_INDEX; 1 x 1 deg): lat_c = floor(lat) + 0.5, lon_c = floor(lon) + 0.5. Nothing is averaged across cells. 'straddles' lists the grids with a cell edge inside the box. A cell's elev_m is the elevation POWER reports with it; for a SYN1deg cell that is the nearest MERRA-2 cell's elevation, not a 1 deg mean, so the cell-gap check uses the MERRA-2 cell. inJordan = share of the cell inside the Natural Earth polygon, from about 0.01 x 0.01 deg samples.

terrain.pixelRule: Open-Meteo's own pixel rule (Dem90.read in Sources/App/Dem/DownloadDem.swift), re-implemented in 32-bit float arithmetic: lati = floor(lat), latrow = trunc(lat * 1200 + 108000) mod 1200, lonrow = trunc((lon + 180) * 1200). On the AWS tiles that is the pixel whose centre is at lat (lati * 1200 + latrow + 1) / 1200, lon (lonrow - 216000) / 1200: 0 to 1 pixel north and west of the point, with no interpolation. Values are rounded to whole metres (Python round, ties to even), as the API returns whole metres; this reproduces every cached Open-Meteo sample of the 5 Jordan sites (checks.controls). Only the index arithmetic is re-implemented; no code is copied.
terrain.methodDetail: statistics from scripts/compute_terrain.py compute_point(), unchanged (see method.text in data/terrain.json); dataset set to copernicus-dem-glo90@aws-cog+open-meteo-pixel-rule; mean_elev_m, mode_elev_m and water_pct added
terrain.waterRule: If flat_water_suspect (at least 20 % of the 441 samples share one elevation) and that elevation is at most -390 m (the Dead Sea and its evaporation ponds) or exactly 0 m (the Gulf of Aqaba), water_pct = the share of samples at it, else 0. water_pct >= 50: terrainExclude ('Mostly water ...') and flag 'water', so terrain and landing are not scored; 20 to 50: flag 'partWater'. Playas (Qa' al-Jafr, Azraq) keep their terrain.
terrain.elevDatum: m above the EGM2008 geoid (Copernicus DEM; horizontal datum WGS84-G1150)

geology.citation: Asch, K. (2005): The 1:5 Million International Geological Map of Europe and Adjacent Areas (IGME5000). Bundesanstalt für Geowissenschaften und Rohstoffe (BGR), Hannover. https://doi.org/10.25928/igme-5000
geology.credit: IGME5000, © BGR, Hannover, 2005, https://doi.org/10.25928/igme-5000, modified: reclassified to Analog Atlas rock ids
geology.scale: 1:5,000,000 (features smaller than a few km are not shown)
geology.sampling: 5 x 5 points per box at -4, -2, 0, +2 and +4 km north and east of the box centre, placed with compute_terrain.destination() on a sphere of R = 6,371,008.8 m and rounded to 6 decimals; each point takes the unit of the IGME5000 polygon that holds it
geology.projection: longitude/latitude -> EPSG:3034 (ETRS89 / LCC Europe, Lambert Conic Conformal 2SP, GRS80) with the formulas of EPSG Guidance Note 7-2, checked on its worked example; WGS84 and ETRS89 are treated as the same (they differ by about 1 m)
geology.dominant: the most frequent unit of the 25 points; ties go to the higher certainty, then the lower unit code
geology.primaryRule: primary = the rock table's primary for the box's unit when its certainty is high or medium; for a low-certainty unit primary is null and the guess is kept as 'inferred' (display only)
geology.secondaryRule: secondary = the rock table's secondaries of the box's unit, plus the primary of every other unit with at least 5 of the 25 points and certainty not low, minus the primary; empty when there is no primary
geology.nullRule: water (8500007) and undifferentiated Neogene (600017) have no rock id
geology.centrePolygon: 0-based record number (shapefile and DBF) of the polygon at the box centre
geology.sameUnitAs: Jordan sites whose own point (data/sites_meta.json) lies in the box's unit
geology.rockTableReview: Awaiting review of every row by a team member.

600016.reason: Cenozoic basalt: maps directly to basalt.

600017.reason: The map gives only an age (Neogene) near Azraq and Wadi Sirhan, and no rock type can be defended from it, so no rock id.

600021.reason: Lake marl of Qa' al-Jafr, read as mudstone (lake mud). The playa's salt is not on the map.

600023.reason: Sandstone listed first; siltstone counts as mudstone. The Wadi Rum unit.

600024.reason: The map gives only an age. Old basement near Aqaba is mostly granite, so granite is a guess.

600061.reason: Granite and granodiorite: maps directly to granite.

600065.reason: The map gives only an age (Precambrian basement at the southern border). Nearby basement units are granite, so granite is a guess.

600069.reason: Marl is listed before limestone and chalk, so carbonate versus mudstone is unclear. A border unit drawn by a neighbouring survey.

600072.reason: Chert only. A thin border unit named by a neighbouring survey (Mount Scopus Group).

600073.reason: Dolomite listed first, so carbonate; marl counts as mudstone. A thin border unit named by a neighbouring survey (Judea Group).

600078.reason: Limestone and dolomite first, so carbonate; shale counts as mudstone and gypsum as evaporite. A thin border unit (Ramon Group).

600080.reason: The map says only 'consolidated siliciclastics' of Precambrian age; sandstone is a broad guess.

600081.reason: Old alkaline volcanic and plutonic rocks. Our rock list has no felsic volcanic class; the plutonic part is closest to granite.

600130.reason: The map gives only an age. Basement near Aqaba is mostly granite, so granite is a guess.

600321.reason: The map gives only an age. Ordovician rocks of the Disi and Rum area are mostly sandstone, so sandstone is a guess.

600322.reason: The map gives only an age. Silurian rocks of south Jordan are sandstone and siltstone, so this is a guess.

601002.reason: Limestone listed first, so carbonate; marl counts as mudstone. Waqf as Suwwan lies in this unit; its crater is too small for the map.

601004.reason: Limestone is listed first, but Jordan's Early Cretaceous is largely sandstone (Kurnub), so the order is a judgement call.

601005.reason: Chalk and limestone are carbonate; marlstone counts as mudstone. The 4th word, phonolite (a volcanic rock), does not fit this sedimentary unit and is ignored.

601007.reason: Mixed sequence with limestone listed first; marl counts as mudstone.

601013.reason: Neogene basalt: maps directly to basalt.

601014.reason: Young basalt: maps directly to basalt. The Harrat site lies in this unit.

601018.reason: Limestone listed first, so carbonate; chert is named by the map; marl counts as mudstone.

601053.reason: Mixed sequence with sandstone listed first; limestone and dolomite give a carbonate secondary.

601056.reason: Sandstone and mudstone, both named by the map.

601062.reason: Rift-valley fill (Jordan Valley, Dead Sea, Wadi Araba). Marl first, so mudstone; loose sand and gravel give a sandstone secondary. The Lisan salt is too small for the map.

8500007.reason: Water: the map shows the Dead Sea and the Gulf of Aqaba as submarine continental crust. No rock id.

flagRules.border: the box crosses the Natural Earth boundary: part of it is outside Jordan (inJordan below 1). The boundary is indicative.
flagRules.cellGap: the NASA POWER MERRA-2 cell is more than 400 m higher or lower than the ground at the box centre (|cellGap_m| > 400, the same rule as cellGap() in js/util.js).
flagRules.climateCellMostlyOutside: less than half of the box's MERRA-2 cell lies in Jordan, so its climate mixes in neighbouring land or sea.
flagRules.straddlesCellEdge: a MERRA-2 or 1 deg SYN1deg cell edge runs through the box; the box takes the cell that holds its centre.
flagRules.partWater: 20 to 50 % of the box is one flat water surface in the elevation data.
flagRules.water: 50 % or more of the box is one flat water surface (the Dead Sea, its evaporation ponds or the Gulf of Aqaba); terrain is not scored (terrainExclude).
flagRules.lowCertaintyGeology: the box's map unit has low certainty, so its rock is shown as 'inferred' and not scored.
flagRules.noGeology: the map has no rock type for the box's unit (water).
